A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COD research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original 70B performance-prediction experiments, component ablations, pilot studies, and continued-pretraining results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds BNSL comparisons, filtering-threshold experiments, and predictions for a 12B model.

M1.justification: The four-stage COD pipeline and cluster-wise fitting formula remain unchanged. v3 generalizes the mapping family and uses a cubic polynomial for the added 12B experiment instead of the quartic default (Section 4.4, Appendix C.2). Cubic interpolation was already ablated in v2; the limited procedural addition is adapting its degree to the available source models.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight main benchmarks, retain the CEval pilot study, and include the continued-pretraining scenario. The 12B experiment changes model configurations within existing task coverage. v3's expanded training-corpus description does not establish an actual change in training data.

E2.justification: v3 adds Broken Neural Scaling Laws (BNSL) to the existing 70B comparison in Table 1 and evaluates it in the new 12B experiment. The three earlier 70B prediction baselines and the existing clustering, interpolation, and anchor comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a 12B-target configuration using only 122M–1.9B source-model passrates, with clustering radius 0.2 and cubic mapping. Appendix C.1 adds controlled threshold variants. Existing benchmark question counts, few-shot settings, and model/token-budget tables remain unchanged; expanded training documentation does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive checks of two previously untested questions: sensitivity to predictable-cluster filtering thresholds, including removing filtering entirely (Appendix C.1), and reliability when prediction relies on smaller source models (Appendix E). Existing clustering, interpolation, anchor, continued-pretraining, and difficulty-distribution analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions describe 100 evaluation attempts and smoothing by averaging across three adjacent checkpoints in Appendix A.2. Neither adds independent training/fitting run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Changes to theoretical variance expressions concern T1, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds BNSL's 70B mean/max errors of 5.17/13.05 percentage points and a complete 12B comparison: mean errors are 4.68 for COD, 14.92 for Loss-intermediate, 10.52 for End-to-end, and 17.42 for BNSL. New threshold results report mean final error 2.36 without thresholds versus 1.63 with baseline filtering. Retained 70B COD results remain 1.63 mean and 2.38 maximum; separate aggregate entries from v2 Table A5 disappear during table consolidation.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix B substantively revise the central assumptions and derivation: accuracy decomposition becomes an explicit assumption instead of being derived through conditional correctness. The theorem's variance correction gains the factor 1/2 already present in v2's proof, while the remainder changes from o(mu) to o(sigma_L^2). v3 also adds a formal prediction problem and computational-complexity analysis. These alter the formal support despite retaining the empirical fitting formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about difficulty clustering, the performance scaling law, and subset-to-full mapping. The claimed 1.36% average error across eight benchmarks for a 70B model is unchanged; additional experiments support the existing contribution framing.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets filtering as important but relatively insensitive to individual thresholds, and attributes larger 12B prediction errors to capabilities remaining unemerged in smaller source models. It also explains adapting polynomial degree to reduce overfitting and argues that inference overhead is small. Existing MoE, evaluation-set-size, and chain-of-thought limitations move from Appendix G to I without substantive revision.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information beyond v2's model tables and brief setup description. Additions include top-p 0.7 and temperature 1.0, clustering radii, corpus-cleaning information, BF16, sequence length 8192, RoPE settings, AdamW hyperparameters, learning-rate/batch-size selection, Megatron, and 52,800 H800 GPU-hours for the 7B model. These are mostly newly disclosed details, not demonstrated changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds BNSL and positions COD against multi-segment power-law approaches. Training documentation adds references for DeepSeek-v2, FineWeb-Edu, GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE, and RMSNorm. The MacQueen citation disappears although K-Means remains evaluated; the broader loss-intermediate versus end-to-end positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the method and proof exposition and reorganizes supporting material. The anchor study moves from Section 5.3.3 to Appendix C.3, supplementary clustering comparisons join the main text, and the appendix sequence changes. A contents listing, Ethics Statement, and Reproducibility Statement are added, replacing the earlier broader-impact paragraph.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, and Figure 4 expands from three panels to eight with BNSL curves. v2 Tables 2, 3, A4, and A5 become one transposed, denser Table 2; new tables present filtering sensitivity and 12B predictions. Existing displays are relocated, and Figure A2's misleading accuracy count-axis label is corrected to sample counts.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional validation through BNSL, filtering sensitivity, and 12B prediction, while filling important implementation gaps. These yield a limited net improvement: the theoretical rewrite leaves the incorrect loss-variance Taylor correction unresolved, and the 1.36% headline still conflicts with Table 1's 1.63%. Table consolidation also introduces misleading aggregation: v3 Table 2 retains four-benchmark summaries beneath eight benchmarks, reporting maximum final error 2.23 despite AGIEval's 2.38.
